To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the strength of the monochromatic gamma ray line from dark matter annihlation is always less than the strength of the continuum gamma ray spectrum from the same annihilation, and that this ratio of line to continuum strength is bounded by a number that is less than one, and is a function of the annihilation channel and mass.

(1) the unitarity relation implies lower limits on the ratio of strength of gamma ray lines to continuum gamma rays; (2) the limits are exact in the case where dark matter annihilates exclusively to one standard model species and in the lowest partial wave; (3) the limits are approximate for more general dark matter annihilations; (4) these limits can be applied to any theory where the gamma ray line is produced through the one-loop process of dark matter annihilation to two photons;

for dark matter annihilation to any single standard model state at tree-level, the strength of the monochromatic gamma ray signal is always smaller than the strength of the continuum gamma ray signal, and this is a universal lower bound that is exact in the limit of a single standard model final state and is valid for any spin of the dark matter particle.
